title: Add interactive RAG prober and compact tool-stub playground
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Authors and integrators need a lightweight, instrumented playground to validate retrieval-agent (RAG) chains without shipping full tool implementations. This PR introduces an "interactive prober" example app and a set of compact tool stubs designed to exercise routing, tool-calling, and telemetry assertions locally. Changes include a tiny local runner, WASM + Node proxy shim, a test prompt suite, telemetry probe hooks, and docs that walk through live assertions and failure injection. What this gives you: 1) A reproducible dev sandbox that simulates tool timeouts, partial outputs, and decontextualized tool results; 2) Clear telemetry hooks for per-step latency and token accounting; 3) A minimal pattern for building compact stubs that can be swapped for real tool bindings in production. High-level changes: added examples/prober/ (runner, UI, probes), examples/stubs/ (http, search, calculator), docs/playgrounds/rag-prober.md, ci/playground-smoke.yaml, tests/prober/e2e-suite.json. How to run locally: 1. yarn install at examples/prober; 2. yarn start to launch the compact UI and runner (defaults to localhost:3002); 3. Use the included scenario files in examples/prober/scenarios to replay recorded traces; 4. Toggle failure-injection flags with ?injectTimeout=true or via the UI to assert graceful fallback behaviour. Checklist: - [x] Example runner implemented and unit tested - [x] Compact stubs and failure injection modes - [x] Documentation and quickstart walkthrough - [x] CI smoke job that runs basic scenarios - [x] Telemetry probes wired into the Console-compatible trace model Backwards compatibility: example-only, no runtime or API surface change to production SDKs or serving runtime. Notes: the prober intentionally uses a smaller dependency set and in-process stubs to remain safe for quickstarts and local dev environments.
